The 90% CI lower bound will sit near 0, so the likely verdict is inconclusive but positively skewed. P(trigger) should be about 30-40% in the top vol tercile vs under 10% in the bottom one (volatility clustering), so the module is worth carrying mainly because the contest starts in a high-vol regime.

hypotheses.definition: Grid of <=12 configs: trigger in {EW <= -4%, z <= -4 (V3)}; ranking in {S1, S2}; exit in {5d fixed, X=6% / H_max=10}; slots in {all-in, staged D=6%} (trim to 12). For each episode e (G=10, 2010-2026), select the config that maximizes the objective over all other episodes, excluding any within ±21 trading days of e, and record the selected config's Delta_e on e. The out-of-episode estimate is the mean and median over e. Also run a chronological version that selects using only episodes before e (fully causal). Report the optimism gap (in-sample best minus out-of-episode) and selection stability (share of folds that pick the modal config).
hypotheses.params: objective in {median Delta_e, mean Delta_e - 0.5 x mean of the worst 3 episodes}; buffer = 21 days; grid <= 12
hypotheses.rationale: IS/VAL/TEST splits hold only about 6-8, 6-8 and 2-4 episodes, and TEST is already seen, so a single IS-best selection is mostly noise. Nested LOEO measures the whole selection procedure, not just one config. The chronological variant mimics what the bot could have known in real time. Stability shows whether any refinement beats the simple default.
hypotheses.expected: Optimism gap of 30-60% of the in-sample Delta. Expanding-window estimate positive but small (+0.5 to +2% per episode at 5d). If stability is below 50%, adopt the simplest default (-4%, S1, 5d, or X1 if it passes the plateau test) or run the panic module at reduced size (staged) rather than a tuned config.

event_studies.trigger: Track A core. Event (i,t): calm_t (x_t > -2%) & no T0 day in [t-5,t] & z_t <= Z & ret1_t <= -R & ret1_t > -20% & not limdown_t. Z in {-2.5,-3.5,-4.5}, R in {4%,7%} = 6 cells per universe. z_t = (clip(ret1_t,+-30%) - b*_t*x_t)/sig_t, where b* is the 120-day shrunk beta (window t-120..t-1) and sig is the 60-day residual RMS (window t-60..t-1, floor 0.008).
event_studies.selection: Universe U200 (ok & caprank<=200) and MIDQ (ok & 200<caprank<=800 & val20_{t-1}>=3e9 & turnover val20_{t-1}/cap_{t-1} <= that day's MIDQ median & not attn20), reported separately. (a) All events equally weighted. (b) Top-2 per day by z ascending, which is what the contest trades. Robustness: top-2 per day by caprank instead of z.
event_studies.entry: Close t (closing auction), and open t+1 (skipped if o_{t+1} >= 1.295*c_t).
event_studies.horizons: 1,3,5,10,21 trading days to the close (close entry: c_{t+h}/c_t; open entry: c_{t+h}/o_{t+1}). All net of 0.35%. For each: excess vs the same-day same-universe EW (same entry and exit), Delta_switch_A = net - r(base_top[t][1]) - 0.35%, median, win rate, date-clustered t-stat (average by date, then t over dates), share of P&L from the top-5 dates, per year, per era (E1..E4), KOSPI vs KOSDAQ, and treated minus a matched same-day placebo (same caprank quintile within the universe, same vol60_{t-1} tercile, |z|<1).

event_studies.trigger: EA1 base event with Z=-3, R=4%. Volume ratio vr_t = val_t/val20_{t-1}, bucketed into DRY vr<=a, MID a<vr<b, SPIKE vr>=b, with (a,b) in {(1.2,3),(1.5,4)}. Quiet 3-day grind variant: c_t/c_{t-3}-1 <= -8% & sum of idio over t-2..t <= -3*sig_t*sqrt(3) & max(val_{t-2..t})/val20_{t-3} <= a. Replication cell: attn20 names & ret1<=-10% & vr>=3 (the knife D6 set) must reproduce a negative 5d return.
event_studies.selection: U200 and MIDQ separately. Also 'quiet large cap': U200 with turnover_{t-1} and vol60_{t-1} both below the U200 median. All events, and top-2 per day by z.

event_studies.trigger: (1) EA1 base event (Z=-3, R=4%). gap_t=o_t/c_{t-1}-1, intra_t=c_t/o_t-1, ibs_t=(c-l)/(h-l) (0.5 if h=l). Mutually exclusive classes: NEWS-GAP gap<=-G & intra<=+0.5%; ABSORB gap<=-G & intra>=+1% & vr>=2; INTRA-LOW gap>=-1% & intra<=-I & ibs<=0.2; INTRA-HI gap>=-1% & intra<=-I & ibs>0.2; OTHER. G, I in {3%,5%}. (2) Wider set: calm & caprank<=500 & ok & ret1<=-8%. G1 gap<=-5% & ibs>=0.6; G2 gap>-2% & ibs<=0.15; G3 locked limit-down (limdown_t & c_t<=l_t*(1+1e-6)).

event_studies.horizons: Overnight (c_t to o_{t+1}), 1, 5, 21; per class: events per year, net mean, median, win rate, excess.

event_studies.trigger: Static 2018 KSIC 'Sector' label (stock_master). secx_{i,t} = mean clip(ret1) of same-sector peers j!=i (c valid, raw>=1000, val20_{t-1}>=1e9); needs >=4 peers, else UNLABELLED. sbreadth = share of peers with ret1<=-3%. Event: calm & ok & ret1<=-R. SINGLE secx>=-1%; SECTOR secx<=-S & sbreadth>=0.5; MIXED otherwise. R in {5%,8%}, S in {2%,4%}. HM-rel5: caprank<=300 & rel5 = ret5_i - median ret5 of sector peers <= -10%. P1 decomposition (caprank<=300 or attn20, ret1<=-e, e in {8%,12%}): M market-driven x<=-m (m in {2%,3%}, cross-track); S sector-driven x>-2% & secx<=-4% & residual>-6%; I idiosyncratic x>-1% & |secx|<2% & residual<=-8%.

event_studies.horizons: 5, 10, 21, plus exit-rule returns: HOLD5, and EXIT-MA (first close >= ma5 from t+1, max 10 days).

event_studies.trigger: nd_t = consecutive down days ending at t (X['down_days']). cum = c_t/c_{t-nd}-1, mcum = M_t/M_{t-nd}-1, icum = cum - b*_t*mcum, worst = min ret1 over the streak. GRIND: U200 & nd>=N & icum<=-X & worst>=-4% & M_t/M_{t-5}-1 > -4%. SHOCK control: U200 & N-day icum<=-X & the single worst day in those N days <= -0.7X. N in {5,7}, X in {6%,10%}.

event_studies.horizons: 5, 21, plus exits HOLD5 and first close >= ma5 (max 7 days).

event_studies.trigger: EA1 base events (Z=-3, R=4%, both universes). Flags at close t: F1 ret1<=-S1 or limdown (S1 in {15%,20%}); F2 ret1_{t-1}<=-10% & ret1_t<=-10%; F3 ret60_{t-1}>=B or max20_{t-1}>=15% (B in {30%,50%}); F4 KOSDAQ label & caprank>300 & date in Mar10-Apr15; F5 raw<2000 or val20_{t-1}<3e9; F6 c_{t-1}/hi250_{t-1}<=0.5. Per-trade net return and average holding days under: E-FIX H in {3,5,10}; E-REC targets {c>=ma5, c>=c_{t0-1}, c>=c_t0+0.5*(c_{t0-1}-c_t0)} x fail overlay {off, on (sell at close if c<l_t0)}, max 10 days; E-TPSL (tp,sl) in {(+5%,-10%),(+8%,-12%)}, intraday, stop fills +0.2% slippage, both hit the same day = stop, max 10. Margin exposure MX_{t-1} = mean of cross-sectional percentile ranks (liquid universe on t-1) of ret60_{t-1}, val20_{t-1}/cap_{t-1} and max20_{t-1}, plus 0.1 if KOSDAQ. Tercile cut-points fixed on IS events.

event_studies.horizons: Common endpoints close t+6 and close t+21. Gap diagnostics g1, g2, g3 = o_{t+k}/c_{t+k-1}-1, and i1 = c_{t+1}/o_{t+1}-1.

event_studies.trigger: Every day with x_t<=-2%, bucketed three ways: (i) x: (-2,-3], (-3,-4], (-4,-5.5], <=-5.5; (ii) zm = x_t/sig_m,t (sig_m = RMS of x over t-60..t-1): (-2,-3], (-3,-4.5], <=-4.5; (iii) K200p z = k200_ret1_t / its own RMS over t-20..t-1, same z buckets.

event_studies.horizons: 1, 5, 10, 21. Episode-clustered means within each bucket (G=10). Spearman correlation of bucket means vs severity. Day-level regression of (c) on |severity| with an episode block-bootstrap 90% CI for the slope. Leave-one-episode-out comparison of which definition better predicts the 5d episode return.

Fixed H in {3,5,7,10,15,21} (plateau curve). X-MKT: exit at the first close with M_u>=M_t0*(1+X), X in {3,6,9}%, H_max in {10,21}. Market stop at M_u<=M_t0*(1-Y), Y in {6,10}%. grid.validation_protocol:
0. RUN AND FREEZE. One script, backtest/lab/panic2.py. It imports engine and panic_sim and extends them: panic_sim.Exit gains fail_low, mkt_tp, mkt_stop, rearm, h_max; Hybrid gains staged, base_off, idx_synthetic, per-config candidate lists, and limit-down deferral. The KSIC file is copied to data/lab/stock_master.csv.gz (FinanceData/stock_master, column 'Sector'). Load market.npz once, use float32 where possible, and compute beta/sigma in blocks of 500 columns.
Phases:
- P0: features and sanity checks.
- P1: all event studies (descriptive).
- P2: IS contest for all 48 configs. Then write backtest/results/lab_panic2_freeze.json with gate outcomes, finalists, the AB composition, the git hash and a sha256.
- P3: VAL for all configs; criteria are applied to the frozen finalists only.
- P4: TEST, run once. The script refuses P4 unless the freeze file exists with an unchanged hash.
Report: backtest/results/lab_panic2.md. No definition, threshold or grid may change after P1 output is viewed. Any change is a new pre-registration, and TEST is then considered spent.

1. COMMON DEFINITIONS. All decisions use data up to the close of the signal day t. Normalizers use windows ending t-1.
- ok_t = c valid & raw>=1000 & val>0 & val20>=1e9 & raw<=300000.
- U200 = ok & caprank<=200. MIDQ as in EA1. attn20 = X['attn20'].
- x_t = mkt_ret1; M = I['mkt'].
- Market z: sig_m,t = sqrt(mean x^2 over t-60..t-1); zm = x/sig_m.
- Beta: r = clip(ret1, +-0.3); beta120 = nan-aware OLS slope of r on x over t-120..t-1, needing >=100 valid days; b* = clip(0.67*beta120+0.33, 0.2, 2.5).
- Residual: idio = r - b*·x; sig = max(0.008, sqrt(mean idio^2 over t-60..t-1)), needing >=40 valid days; z = idio/sig.
- vr = val/val20_{t-1}; gap, intra, ibs as in EA3.
- Lim = 0.15 before 2015-06-15, else 0.30; limdown = c <= c_{t-1}*(1-Lim+0.005).
- T0 = x<=-4%.
- base_top = the R0 ranking. The base holding sold first is the one with the worst base rank; a name missing from the list counts as worst.
- Delta_switch(h): B = basket net (0.35% cost) minus mean gross return of base_top[t][:2] over the same window, minus 0.35%. A = event net minus base_top[t][1] gross, minus 0.35%.
- Episodes: panic_sim.episodes with G=10 (sensitivity G=5, 21), used for aggregation only.
- Eras: E1 2010.07-2015.06.12; E2 2015.06.15-2018; E3 2019-2024.09; E4 2024.10-2026.09.
- Market label: static per stock, a minor look-ahead that is noted.

2. COSTS AND SIM. Event studies use a 0.35% round trip. Contest sims use engine costs: fee 0.015% each side, tax 0.20%, slippage max(0.05%, half tick) per side, +0.2% on intraday stops. The synthetic index pays no tax and has a 5-won tick. The account is 600k with k=2 slots and integer shares. No buy when open or close >= 1.295 x the prior close. Limit-down deferral is ON in all runs except the R1 replication.
Starts:
- IS: 2011-01-03..2018-12-28, every 2 trading days.
- VAL: 2019-01-02..2024-09-30, every 2 trading days.
- TEST: 2024-10-01..T-21, every day.
Each window is 21 sessions and is liquidated at the last close. Per config and period, report: mean, median, P10d = P(month<=-10%), P10u, CVaR10, worst month, trades per month, share of windows with an mp or sp entry, mean with and without entries, and the last 12 months (descriptive).

3. SANITY (P0; the script stops if any fails).
- R1 replication with deferral OFF reproduces lab_panic.md (IS +0.9%, VAL +0.6%, TEST +5.5%) within +-0.2pp.
- For every hybrid config, Delta = config - R0 per start is exactly 0 on windows with no signal in [s-1, e-1].
- Print trigger days per year for every trigger, and sector-label coverage of U200 per year.

4. EVENT GATES (IS 2011-2018 only; they decide eligibility, not ranking).
Track A: each trigger's contest entry with a 5-day fixed exit must meet all of:
- >=200 events in >=100 distinct weeks;
- median net > 0;
- mean excess vs the same-day same-universe EW > 0 with date-clustered t >= 2.0;
- top-5 dates < 40% of total net P&L;
- no calendar year > 35% of P&L;
- mean of (treated - matched placebo) > 0.
Configs whose trigger fails are ineligible. If no track-A trigger passes, track A has no finalists and the report concludes that the stock-specific panic edge is not tradable at this size.
Track B: each (trigger, selection, entry) at the config's horizon (FIX H; 10 for X-MKT) must meet all of:
- >=4 IS episodes;
- IS episode-mean Delta_switch > 0;
- IS share of episodes with Delta > 0 >= 50%.
Fixed-H configs also need a plateau: the IS episode means at H-2 and H+2 have the same sign and at least 50% of the magnitude at H (from the EB6 curve; H=5 uses H in {3,7}; H=10 uses {7,15}).

5. IS SELECTION. J = mean - 0.2*P10d (fractions). A config is eligible if it passes its gate, J_IS > J_IS(R0), and P10d_IS <= P10d_IS(R0) + 0.02. Finalists are the top-3 by J_IS per track, plus AB_combo if both tracks have an IS #1. That is at most 7 finalists. R0, R1 and A18 are references and never eligible. The freeze JSON is written here.

6. VAL PASS (all required, finalists only; Delta = config - R0 on identical starts).
- (i) mean_VAL - mean_VAL(R0) >= +0.30pp.
- (ii) P10d_VAL <= P10d_VAL(R0) + 0.01.
- (iii) Leave-one-out:
  - Track B: for each VAL episode e of the config's own trigger (G=10), drop every start whose window contains an entry signal of e. The minimum over e of mean Delta must be > 0.
  - Track A: leave one calendar year out (2019..2024), minimum > 0. Also drop starts containing the 5 dates with the largest sp P&L; the remaining mean Delta must be > 0.
- (iv) Pooled IS+VAL:
  - Track B: mean Delta without the top-2 episodes > 0, and the share of episodes with Delta_e > 0 >= 50%.
  - Track A: the share of VAL quarters with mean Delta > 0 >= 55%.
- (v) Placebo (pooled IS+VAL, 200 draws), real mean Delta >= the 80th percentile:
  - Track B: fire the same overlay on matched placebo days (EB7 matching, same count per year).
  - Track A: same entry dates, but 1 random U200 name with ret1<=0 and |z|<1.
- (vi) AB_combo must also have VAL mean >= max(single components) - 0.2pp, and P10d no more than 1pp above the better single.
Among VAL passers in each track, adopt the one with the highest pooled IS+VAL J. VAL is never used to rank non-finalists.

7. TEST (once, after the freeze).
Pass (a veto only): mean_TEST >= mean_TEST(R0) AND P10d_TEST <= P10d_TEST(R0) + 0.02.
Track B's TEST is contaminated, because lab_panic.md already saw 2024.10-2026.09 including 17 T0 days in 2026. So track B's TEST can only veto, never promote. Also report TEST excluding the 2026-03 episode, and TEST for all finalists (for transparency only).

8. ADOPTION. A track's config is adopted only if it passes gate + IS selection + all VAL criteria + the TEST veto. If nothing passes, the bot stays R0, with no panic module.
Labels:
- 'strong' if the episode block-bootstrap (5000 resamples, pooled IS+VAL) 90% CI lower bound of E[Delta_e] is > 0;
- otherwise 'weak / positively skewed'.

9. DIAGNOSTICS (reported, never gates):
- Nested chronological leave-one-episode-out over the eligible B configs (expanding window, >=5 prior episodes): out-of-episode mean and median, optimism gap, and selection stability.
- Module value = P(>=1 trigger in 21 days | mkt_vol20 tercile at start) x E[Delta | trigger], evaluated at the tercile of 2026-09-23.
- Month-end split (panic entry with <3 sessions left vs more).
- Close-entry robustness: the same config with the entry moved to the next open.
- Leave-one-out with G=5 and G=21.
- 2019+ subset for sector-based configs.
- Episode-level tables (N_ep, mean, median, share>0, worst, leave-one-out min/max, mean without the best 1 and 2) for every B config.

critique:
1. **Halted days leak (the most serious one).** Halted days are still rows in `market.npz`: Volume is 0 and open/high/low are set to the stale close. In marcap 2020 there are 22,477 such rows, every one with Open=0. About 100 codes sit in a halt of more than 30 days just before delisting. `run_month_hybrid` fills an order whenever `c>0`, so the sim buys and sells at stale prices during halts. FIX and REC exits therefore get out of names that were actually frozen, and knife events are enriched in exactly those names.
   - Allow no fill on a day with `val==0`, and require `val_{t+1}>0` for open entries.
   - A position that cannot be sold keeps its slot. Its cash is not recycled.
   - Event-study forward returns use the first traded close on or after t+h.
   - At window end, report both the stale mark and the first traded price after the halt.
   - Report, per config, the share of events that hit a halt within 21 days.

2. **Static labels are a look-ahead we can remove.** `build_marcap` keeps the last `Market` value per stock. 22 codes moved from KOSDAQ to KOSPI (for example Celltrion 2018, Kakao 2017). The daily `Market` column is still in `scratchpad/marcap/data/*.parquet`.
   - Build a point-in-time T×N market label. Use it for K200p, KOSDAQ-L (B17), `is_kosdaq`, F4, the MX +0.1 term and every KOSPI/KOSDAQ split.
   - The sector labels are a 2018-11 snapshot: delisted names are included, but every IPO after 2018 is missing, so coverage falls to 70% by 2026. Treat unlabelled names as their own group rather than dropping them in S-SECREL, A17 and EA4.
   - Add a control run of K2 and SA1 restricted to labelled names. This shows whether an edge is just "exclude young IPOs".

3. **Cash-dividend ex-dates create fake shocks.** KRX does not adjust the base price for cash dividends, so ex-dividend drops stay in `ret1`. High-yield U200 names (banks, holding companies, telecoms, insurers) print z≤−3.5 and ret1≤−4% on a flat-market ex-date, and these drops do not revert.
   - Through 2022, exclude the December ex-date (the second-to-last trading day of the year) and the day after it from all track-A triggers.
   - Add an EA7 flag: 3 or more same-sector U200 financials each down at least 3% on a calm day in December, or in February to April after the 2023 record-date reform.
   - Report how many events this removes.

4. **Rules that need the exact final close.** These rules cannot be known at 15:19:
   - CF_A "not limdown"
   - A04/A10 C1 (c_t≥c_{t−1}, l_t≥l_{t−1})
   - EA3 G3 (locked limit-down)
   - REC exit (c_u≥ma5_u, where ma5_u includes c_u; FAIL uses c<l_t0)
   - X-MKT and market stop evaluated at the close
   - T6 close-u* entry (x_u≥+1%)
   - B19 (T0 at the close)
   - vr thresholds: a 15:19 reading misses the closing-auction volume.

   Required changes:
   - (a) For each close-decided config, recompute the decision inputs from c·(1+ε), with ε~N(0, 0.4%) per stock plus a common market term, and use vr·0.9. Keep filling at the true close. Run 50 draws; the config stays eligible only if at least 75% of its IS Delta survives.
   - (b) State how the live bot computes x_t and M_u at 15:19: about 1,500 names through the KIS multi-quote API, or a cap-weighted index proxy. Backtest that exact definition.
   - (c) Make "close decisions moved to the next open, sign preserved" a required check, not a diagnostic.
   - (d) Define U200, MIDQ and KOSDAQ-L membership with `caprank_{t−1}`.

5. **Contamination has to be declared.**
   - Track B's VAL is not clean. F-a, F-c, the market stop, staged entry and T6 were designed after `lab_panic` showed VAL failing because the 2020 and 2022 panics kept falling. TEST was also already seen.
   - Make the nested chronological leave-one-episode-out a required criterion for track B, not a diagnostic. It uses an expanding window and reruns the whole selection inside each fold. Across all 2011–2026.9 episodes, the out-of-episode mean Delta must be above 0 and the median at least 0.
   - Note that track A's volume-dry-up and capitulation ideas came from the full-sample knife study (2015–2026, which includes VAL and TEST).

6. **Protocol hygiene.**
   - Run P1 event studies on IS dates only until the freeze file is written. Produce the VAL and TEST columns in P3 and P4. Otherwise people see VAL results before any fix or re-registration, for example after a P0 failure.
   - R1 replication: import `panic.run_hybrid` and compare it with `panic_sim` start by start, rather than checking against the rounded numbers in the report.
   - List the known behaviour differences in advance. For example, when no candidate fills, `panic.py` holds cash for H days, while `panic_sim` goes back to the base strategy. A mismatch then cannot lead to ad-hoc code edits.

7. **Too many degrees of freedom in track B.** There are 27 configs and roughly 10 IS episodes.
   - (a) In P0, compute each trigger's IS day-overlap (Jaccard) with T0. Any trigger at 0.6 or above (probably T1, T2, T3, T5) is merged into T0 and is not eligible on its own.
   - (b) The gate needs at least 6 IS episodes and at least 5 VAL episodes. Filtered variants that fall below this (F-a, F-c) are "untestable".
   - (c) Allow at most one finalist per trigger family and one per exit family. FIX10, X-MKT and X-MKT-STOP trade the same entries.
   - (d) Run the combos B25–B27 only if each component passed the IS gate.

8. **No control for picking the best of many configs.** Choosing the top 3 by J_IS from 27 and 18 configs has no family-wise protection.
   - Add an IS reality check at the episode level using vectorised Delta_switch. Fire every eligible config on EB7-matched placebo days 1,000 times and record, per draw, the best config's episode-mean Delta. A finalist must beat the 90th percentile of that maximum.
   - Do the same for track A with the random-placebo-name draw.
   - VAL criterion (v): raise it from the 80th percentile of 200 draws to the 90th percentile of at least 1,000.

9. **Hidden confound from mid-month re-ranking.** R0 only rotates at the window start (window = 21 days). After a panic exit the hybrid sets `next_rebal=t+1`, so it gets a fresh re-ranking of the base book that R0 never gets. The track-A refill after an event exit does the same.
   - Add a control R0-REFRESH: same trigger days, keep base through the H days, then rebalance on the same date as the hybrid.
   - Add the equivalent control for track A.
   - VAL (i) and the pooled leave-one-out must also pass against these controls.

10. **Track-A gate statistics.**
    - Clustering by date on overlapping 5-day and 21-day returns understates the standard error. Use Newey–West with lag h−1 on the daily-mean series, or non-overlapping calendar weeks as EA4 already does.
    - Add Delta_switch_A>0 with t≥2. The real alternative to an event trade is the base holding it replaces, not the EW market.
    - Require the mean excess to be positive in E1 (±15% limit) and E2 separately, because the limit regime changes which drops are excluded as limit-down.

11. **Missing market-panic stock choices.** Add three contest cells, all T0 / open t+1 / FIX5, paid for by the triggers deleted in item 7 so the config count does not grow:
    - **S-BETA:** highest b* among U200 names with ret1 at or below the U200 median. This is the clean beta bet that K2 only approximates.
    - **S-MEGA:** caprank≤30 and raw price ≤300k, deepest ret1.
    - **K2-EP:** rank by drawdown over the episode, c_t/max(c_{t−10..t})−1, instead of the one-day ret1.

12. **Missing knife alternatives.**
    - (a) Opening-gap fade, which daily data can test. Condition: gap_t≤−G with G in {4, 7}%, idiosyncratic gap (gap−b*·EWgap)/sig≤−3, and EW gap above −1%. Buy just after 09:00 at o_t with +0.3% extra slippage. Exits: close t, close t+1 or FIX5. Add it as EA3b plus one A config.
    - (b) Non-fundamental calendar drops, expected to revert more: option expiry days, KOSPI200 June/December rebalancing, MSCI rebalancing days. Add as a positive EA7 flag.

13. **Stock-status data we don't have.** There is no history of administrative designation (관리종목), investment warning/risk (투자경고/위험), short-term overheating single-price trading (단기과열/단일가) or delisting liquidation trading (정리매매). Knife names are enriched in these, the contest may bar them, and single-price trading changes close fills.
    - Backtest proxy: exclude from track A any name with a `val==0` day or a limit-down day in [t−20, t−1]. Report the effect.
    - Live: check stock status through the KIS API before any event or panic buy, and specify the fallback candidate order.

14. **Risk and adoption metrics.** J = mean − 0.2·P10d over all windows dilutes the risk: triggers fire in about 10% of windows. Two changes:
    - Also compute P10d and CVaR10 only on windows that contain a module entry. Require conditional CVaR10 ≥ R0's minus 2pp, in both IS and VAL.
    - Make the final adopt / don't-adopt call on this: P(trigger in the contest month, given the current mkt_vol20 tercile) × pooled out-of-episode Delta must be at least 0.30pp.
